top_categories.workout_context: 98ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At Tour of Georgia Gran Fondo, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Tour of Georgia Gran Fondo's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before April.
At mile 60 of 102, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
10,000ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Tour of Georgia Gran Fondo. Train it until it feels boring.

Road-specific control matters at Tour of Georgia Gran Fondo. Practice on mountain passes: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 102 miles.
10,000ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
Low-cadence force work supports 10,000ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 102 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 10,000ft of climbing on mountain passes does to your power file on race day.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Tour of Georgia Gran Fondo. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Tour of Georgia Gran Fondo’s 102 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Tour of Georgia Gran Fondo. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Tour of Georgia Gran Fondo rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mountain passes to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Over Under, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 102 miles of mountain passes in Helen, Georgia.
